system:
You are the Arabic language reviewer, standing in for an Arabic reviewer at the issuing authority. You compare the Arabic text with the English text and report any difference in meaning: numbers, times, places, the hazard, and above all the protective action. You cannot approve the Arabic; a named person who reads Arabic still must.
You see only the English and Arabic headline, description and instruction, and how the Arabic was produced. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

[CAPCP#0035] Canadian Profile of the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP-CP): Introduction and Rule Set 1.0 (Draft 2) (Constraint of one subject event per alert message):
Constraint of one subject event per alert message The Reference Standard allows for the inclusion of multiple subject events within a single CAP alert message, but specifies only one unique CAP message identifier is required. Therefore, a situational change to any one of the subject events, triggering a new CAP message update, would give the appearance of a change to any and all of the other subject events within the update message. Further, given that event values will be used for the purpose of filtering, routing, validating, and other needs within the community; systems could have difficulty handling a single alert message containing multiple subject events when the information associated to a subset of the subject events may be changing. To avoid any potential confusion, the CAP-CP limits each CAP alert message to one subject event value.

data.summary: The Arabic matches the English in meaning: the fog hazard, zero visibility, western regions of the UAE, the times (21:30 Tue 17 Feb to 10:00 Wed 18 Feb), the source (NCM), the driving instructions and the URL all carry over. The dam-burst sentence and 'leave the area now' are also rendered faithfully ('تفيد التقارير بانهيار سد قرب العين؛ غادروا المنطقة فوراً'). One issue needs a person: the Arabic came from machine translation, so a named Arabic reader must check it before release. I cannot approve it. Separately, there is a concern outside my translation mandate. The alert carries an unverified dam-burst report and an evacuation order inside a fog warning, in both languages. Approvers should look at this.

objections.issue: The Arabic text was produced by machine translation and has had no human Arabic review. Machine-translated alert text carries a known risk of material inaccuracy. My comparison does not replace sign-off by a named Arabic-reading reviewer at the issuing authority.
objections.fix: Before release, a named Arabic-reading reviewer at the issuing authority must check and approve the Arabic headline, description and instruction. Pay particular attention to the protective actions: 'قُد بحذر شديد' and 'غادروا المنطقة فوراً'.

the accuracy of a translation requires human intervention

no_basis.concern: Both language versions contain an unverified second hazard: 'Reports say a dam near Al Ain has burst'. It comes with an evacuation order ('leave the area now') inside a fog warning. That order conflicts with the fog instruction to drive carefully. The translation of this sentence is faithful, so this is a content problem, not a translation one. Approvers should confirm whether this sentence belongs in the alert at all.

no_basis.concern: The Arabic uses singular imperatives in the instruction ('قُد', 'حافظ', 'التزم') but a plural imperative in the description ('غادروا'). This is a stylistic inconsistency only, not a difference in meaning.
